title: Slider Responsiveness
question: Why isn't a slider instant yet? A slider release on the Kids' Choice slide costs under a millisecond in the plain-JS Dress Up app and 4.6 s in Hazel on 2026-10-09: this report collects every performance problem found and fixed this fall, then looks at where the remaining time of a release goes and what it would take to get to "immediate".

headline.what: Dress Up (plain JS): one slider change, update and re-render
Kids' Choice: a slider release until the face redraws (now; median of 12, two runs)
Polygons: a click adding a point (was ~11 s)

measures.release to face: ms or s, wall time: from the slider's change event until the face's eyes redraw at the new size (Kids' Choice, the eye-size slider)
measures.profiled stage times: ms, profiled: CPU time per release in each part of the page and the worker, from the Gecko profiler; profiled times are about 1.5× real ones (the profile sections) or 1.7× (the method), and code made of many small calls looks several times costlier under the profiler
measures.the worker's time per release: ms, profiled: deciding what to reuse (reuse_check), evaluating, encoding
measures.request and response size: KB: the encoded message posted to or from the eval worker (Worker.prototype.postMessage wrapped after load; request sizes for the diff requests from a temporary probe on the encoded message in post_evaluate)
measures.the face's view evaluation: ms: one evaluation of the face livelit's view, warm (see runs)
measures.the face's first evaluation after a rele: ms: with and without the call memo
measures.view building per redraw: ms: each redraw's own view building (preview, commit, face, final result)
measures.re-evaluation after one edit (dev benchm: ms: a 400-definition program, evaluated, then its last literal edited with every id kept; only the incremental re-evaluation is timed
measures.evaluator benchmark: ms, min and median of 15 evaluations: a program that builds a 2,000-element list of tuples through recursive helpers and recurses 3,000 deep, run through evaluate_open
measures.loading a slide: s: Shoes and Hair, Shirt and Pants
measures.Dress Up slider change: ms: one input event, update and re-render; median 0 ms, worst 2 ms, at Firefox's 1 ms timer resolution
measures.Polygons click: s: a click adding a point
measures.the table of problems (#issues): each row's Measured cell, as printed, in its own unit. Many rows were measured on other slides and benchmarks (nested lets, a parser corpus, Shirt and Pants, Shoes and Hair, Polygons); the report gives no method for them beyond the row. Details and discussion: hazelgrove/hazel#2609, findings 10 and 11.

times: Wall times: from the slider's change event until the face's eyes redraw at the new size (scripts/slider_timing.py; scripts/release_timing.py without the debug panel). Timelines wrap the page's Worker.postMessage, listen to the worker's messages, and watch the face's eye with a MutationObserver, timing each against the release. Stage times: the Gecko profiler, started from Firefox's privileged context after load and bracketed with performance.mark (scripts/profile_interaction.py). Message sizes: scripts/worker_sizes.py. Firefox timers have 1 ms resolution.
provenance: No raw readings of this report survive: every number exists only as printed in the page, in its tables (tables.json) and its drawn figures (figures, below). The CPU profiles behind the profiled tables are not in this repository, nor are the drivers named above (the report: untracked scripts in a local Hazel checkout).

figures.note: The numbers this page's drawn figures show, copied from the page's own SVG and script on 2026-10-14 (not a measurement log; no raw readings behind them survive). Times in ms unless a field says s.

race.what: One Kids' Choice slider release, Hazel against Dress Up, animated in real time. Both lanes start when the slider is released and finish when the picture shows the new value.

memo.label: before the last three steps (0.17 s)

race.dress_up_ms: under 1 (the lane is drawn as 1 ms)
race.lane_totals_are: the median wall time without the profiler. The three newest (now, memo, diff) are each the mean of two twelve-release medians measured without the debug panel: 140 and 142 ms now; 163.5 and 179 ms before the last three steps; 229 and 273 ms with the diff requests.
race.stage_split_is: the CPU profile of one release (ms, profiled), used only as proportions of the lane: the views lane as listed, the hash lane with the worker at 145 instead of 410 (the page's script). The now, memo, diff and before lanes are one colour: their stages were not split out the same way.

pipeline.what: Hazel, one slider release, to scale (CPU profile; real time is about 1.7× shorter). The 10-10 afternoon profile, at 0.43 s a release, before the diff requests.
main_thread_ms_profiled: handle the event: the livelit's update
re-build terms for the changed item (MakeTerm)
build and encode the worker request: the whole program, 478 KB
decode and merge the worker's results, up to 383 KB
redraw: evaluate livelit views (now cached for unchanged models)
redraw: Hazel rebuilding its view in JavaScript, over several redraws, and frame callbacks (the browser's own layout and DOM work is ~30 ms of it)
pipeline.dress_up: input → update one field → re-render the SVG: under 1 ms, start to finish

reuse_check_worker.what: The eval worker, per Kids' Choice slider release (CPU profile), before the reuse-check fix.

progress.what: Kids' Choice slider release, seconds (headless Firefox, no profiler, median of 4), after each fix.
progress.immediate_is: the usual threshold for an action to feel instant
progress.starred_bars: measured differently: without the debug panel, median of 12 releases, two runs (the two numbers in brackets); the build before the first of them measured 0.36 s the same way.
progress.noise: Runs vary by about ±0.07 s, so the reuse-check step is smaller than the noise in any one run; the worker's own time (410 → 145 ms profiled) is the steadier measure.
progress.fix_column_from: the report's table of problems (#issues), whose Measured cells give these steps: Kids' Choice 4.6 → 1.6 s, 1.6 → 0.8 s, 0.8 → 0.53 s; the request 478 → 18.5 KB with release to face 359 → 229–273 ms. The step '+ evaluator, views, result index' gathers several rows of that table (7a5667e6f2, 857c293962, 2d35bb9e01, 602498d7aa, c64c558e86, 42902c2d2a) and is left without a fix here.
